issues.legal_issue: Pure factual findings on a landlord’s bona fide requirement and comparative hardship are not disturbed on appeal when they are supported by the fact-finding authority’s assessment.
material_facts: The prescribed authority considered the parties’ pleadings and evidence and found that the landlords bona fide required the shop and would suffer greater hardship if it were not released to them.
The appellate court affirmed those findings, and the tenants challenged them before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court declined to disturb the findings on bona fide requirement and comparative hardship because they were findings of fact.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the prescribed authority’s findings on bona fide requirement and comparative hardship as pure findings of fact and held that they could not be upset in this appeal. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.eviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an eviction order.
predicates.bona_fide_requirement_found_on_evidence: The fact-finding authority assessed the evidence and found that the landlord genuinely required the premises.
predicates.comparative_hardship_found_on_evidence: The fact-finding authority assessed the evidence and found that refusing eviction would cause the landlord greater hardship than granting it would cause the tenant.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal concerns findings reached after assessment of evidence on genuine need and comparative hardship, those pure factual findings are not disturbed.

issues.legal_issue: A court reviewing an eviction proceeding must consider a material subsequent event that may affect the claimed personal requirement, even when the event occurs during writ review.
material_facts: The eviction application was based on the landlords’ need to conduct a business in the shop.
Both landlords died while the writ petition was pending, and that event was brought to the High Court’s attention.
The landlords’ three daughters were substituted, and the tenants relied on the fact that they were married and living at their marital homes.
The High Court refused to consider the deaths, reasoning that it could not take account of subsequent events in writ proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in law and jurisdiction by refusing to consider the landlords’ deaths. The Supreme Court set aside its order and remitted the matter for consideration of the subsequent event and the applicable law.
issues.legal_principle: Ordinarily, parties’ rights are determined as at the institution of the proceeding. However, a court may, and where appropriate must, take cautious account of subsequent events if the original relief has become inappropriate, consideration can shorten litigation, or it is needed to do complete justice, subject to procedural fairness and prompt notice. A personal requirement must continue until final determination. The Court relied on Shikharchand Jain v. Digamber Jain Praband Karini Sabha, Pasupuleti Venkateswarlu v. Motor & General Traders, Om Prakash Gupta v. Ranbir B. Goyal, and Hasmat Rai v. Raghunath Prasad. It distinguished Rameshwar v. Jot Ram, which concerned agrarian reforms, and Gaya Prasad v. Pradeep Srivastava, where the relevant need was not extinguished in the same way.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding and personal_requirement_basis and landlord_died_during_review and material_subsequent_event_brought_to_court and (relief_may_become_inappropriate or consideration_may_shorten_litigation or consideration_needed_for_complete_justice)

predicates.eviction_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a claim to evict a tenant from premises.
predicates.personal_requirement_basis: The landlord seeks eviction on the basis of a personal requirement for the premises.
predicates.landlord_died_during_review: The landlord whose personal requirement supports the eviction claim died while judicial review of the claim was pending.
predicates.material_subsequent_event_brought_to_cou: A subsequent event capable of affecting the claimed need was brought to the reviewing court’s attention.
predicates.relief_may_become_inappropriate: The subsequent event may make the relief originally sought inappropriate.
predicates.consideration_may_shorten_litigation: Considering the subsequent event may shorten the litigation.
predicates.consideration_needed_for_complete_justic: Considering the subsequent event may be necessary to do complete justice between the parties.

issues.definition: When a material subsequent event affecting a personal-requirement eviction claim is brought to the reviewing court and one of the stated purposes for considering it applies, the court must consider that event.

issues.legal_issue: After a landlord dies while a personal-requirement release application is pending, the landlord’s legal representatives may continue the proceeding on the basis of their own need in substitution for the deceased landlord’s need.
material_facts: The release application sought possession on the ground of the landlords’ bona fide requirement.
Both landlords died while the litigation was pending, and their three daughters were brought on record as legal representatives.
The tenants argued that the deceased landlords’ requirement no longer survived.
issues.conclusion: The legal representatives could prosecute the application on the basis of their own need in substitution for the deceased landlords’ need; the High Court had to consider that provision and make a finding on remand.
issues.legal_principle: The Court read Section 21(1)(a) together with Section 21(7) of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972. Where possession is sought on the ground of bona fide requirement and the landlord dies during the pendency of the application, the legal representatives may prosecute it on the basis of their own need in substitution for the deceased landlord’s need. The Court also referred to Hasmat Rai v. Raghunath Prasad.

rule.if: eviction_release_proceeding and personal_requirement_basis and landlord_died_while_claim_pending and legal_representatives_brought_on_record

predicates.eviction_release_proceeding: The proceeding is an application seeking release of rented premises from a tenant.
predicates.personal_requirement_basis: The application seeks possession on the basis of the landlord’s personal bona fide requirement.
predicates.landlord_died_while_claim_pending: The landlord died while the claim for release was pending.
predicates.legal_representatives_brought_on_record: The landlord’s legal representatives were brought into the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a landlord dies during a pending release claim based on personal requirement and legal representatives are brought into the proceeding, they may continue the claim on the basis of their own need.
